source.description: Expert DAG from the published MIMIC-IV target-trial emulation this study replicates, built by the paper's own authors with a clinician using DAGitty (dagitty.net), per the paper's methods section.
source.figure: S6 Fig, "Directed Acyclic Graph" (Fig 1 in the supplement: "Causal graph for the Albumin vs crystalloids emulated trial")
source.transcribed_by: manual transcription of the S6 Fig PDF supplied by the user
transcription_notes: Every node in the figure sends an edge to both the treatment and the outcome (a dense confounder fan; the figure caption states only the most important edges are drawn from an expert point of view) -- encoded here as role='confounder' for every node, except the two relations noted below.

Gray nodes in the figure (Socio-economical factor, Comorbidity, lifestyle) are captioned 'not controlled for since they are not available in the data' -- encoded here as observed=false confounders, not omitted, so identification checks see them as a real (unobservable) backdoor path rather than as absent from the model.

Two edges (Comorbidity -> SOFA, Comorbidity -> SAPSII) are visually distinct short arrows breaking from the dominant long-arrow fan pattern and are transcribed with moderate, not full, confidence -- not independently re-verified against a higher-resolution render of the PDF.

AKI stage and Dialysis (RRT) are encoded as plain confounders like every other node. The figure may draw a more specific relationship between the two (e.g. AKI severity preceding RRT initiation), but this could not be read with confidence from the available render and was deliberately not invented -- verify directly against the source PDF before relying on this pair specifically.

Node labels are taken verbatim from the figure and do not necessarily match this study's own protocol.json wording (e.g. figure 'Albumin + crystalloids' vs protocol.json's longer target_trial.treatment string) -- structural_hamming_distance/structural_intervention_distance compare graphs at the node-label level (see causal.agents.dag_metrics), so any future generated candidate_dag must use labels that at least approximately match these for a comparison to be meaningful.
